budgets.name: Frugal
budgets.note: Hostels, guesthouses, self-catering, regional trains and buses.

budgets.name: Comfortable
budgets.note: Three-star hotels or good apartments, one restaurant meal a day, some fast trains.

budgets.name: Generous
budgets.note: Well-reviewed hotels, restaurants that book out, flights and first-class rail where it saves a day.

cities.name: Theth
cities.why: A valley village of stone houses with no road in until recently, a lock-in tower, and a waterfall above it.
highlights: The Valbona-Theth pass, a six-hour crossing on foot
The kulla, a tower where men under blood feud could shelter

cities.name: Gjirokastër
cities.why: A UNESCO-listed Ottoman town of stone-roofed tower houses on a steep hillside under a castle.
highlights: Slate-roofed houses built as fortified homes
The castle, and the American spy plane parked in it

cities.name: Himarë & the Riviera
cities.why: Ionian villages between mountain and sea, with beaches that were empty ten years ago and are filling fast.
highlights: Gjipe beach, at the mouth of a canyon, reached on foot
The Llogara pass, dropping 1,000 metres to the sea

cities.name: Tirana
cities.why: A capital whose mayor painted the grey communist blocks in primary colours, and where a nuclear bunker is now a museum.
highlights: Bunk'Art: Hoxha's nuclear bunker, 106 rooms, as a museum
The Pyramid, a dictator's mausoleum turned tech centre

cities.name: Andorra la Vella
cities.why: Europe's highest capital at 1,023 metres, in a narrow valley, mostly shops with mountains directly behind them.
highlights: Casa de la Vall, the 16th-century parliament house
Caldea thermal spa, fed by hot springs

cities.name: Madriu-Perafita-Claror
cities.why: A glacial valley with no road into it, on the UNESCO list for a cultural landscape of summer pasture and stone huts.
highlights: Nine per cent of the country, entered only on foot
Shepherds' bordes and dry-stone terraces still standing

cities.name: Dilijan
cities.why: A forested spa town called 'Armenian Switzerland', with two of the country's finest monasteries in the woods nearby.
highlights: Haghartsin and Goshavank monasteries in deep forest
The Transcaucasian Trail through the national park

cities.name: Tatev
cities.why: A 9th-century monastery on a cliff in the far south, reached by the world's longest reversible cable car.
highlights: The Wings of Tatev cable car, 5.7 km over a gorge
The monastery's swinging pillar, an early seismograph

cities.name: Garni & Geghard
cities.why: A Hellenistic temple on a gorge, and a monastery partly carved out of the rock face next door.
highlights: Garni: the only Greco-Roman colonnaded temple left in the former Soviet Union
Geghard's rock-cut chambers and their acoustics

cities.name: Yerevan
cities.why: A capital rebuilt in pink volcanic stone to a 1924 plan, with Ararat filling the southern horizon.
highlights: The Cascade, a stairway of terraces and sculpture
Matenadaran, a library of 17,000 medieval manuscripts

cities.name: Hallstatt
cities.why: A lakeside village under a salt mountain, with 7,000 years of continuous mining and more visitors than it can hold.
highlights: The oldest salt mine in the world, and a wooden staircase from 1344 inside it
The bone house, with painted skulls stacked by family

cities.name: Salzburg
cities.why: Baroque built on salt money, under a fortress, with Mozart born in the middle of it.
highlights: Hohensalzburg fortress, never taken in a thousand years
Mozart's birthplace and the concerts in the Residenz

cities.name: Innsbruck
cities.why: A university city at 574 metres with a 2,300-metre mountain reachable from the centre in twenty minutes.
highlights: The Nordkette funicular, Zaha Hadid stations from town to summit
The Golden Roof and the old town beneath it

cities.name: Dürnstein & the Wachau
cities.why: A blue baroque tower over the Danube, terraced vineyards behind, and the castle where Richard the Lionheart was held.
highlights: Grüner Veltliner and Riesling from terraces built by monks
The Danube cycle path, flat and shaded

cities.name: Vienna
cities.why: Habsburg on the outside, Freud and Klimt and social housing on the inside, with the world's best-funded music scene.
highlights: Klimt's Kiss at the Belvedere and the Secession's Beethoven Frieze
Standing tickets at the Staatsoper for the price of a sandwich

cities.name: Baku
cities.why: A UNESCO-listed walled city with a mysterious stone tower, ringed by oil-boom mansions and three flame-shaped skyscrapers.
highlights: Icherisheher, the walled old city, and the Maiden Tower nobody can fully explain
The Heydar Aliyev Centre, Zaha Hadid's curved white building

cities.name: Sheki
cities.why: A silk road town under wooded mountains, with a khan's summer palace whose windows are built without glue or nails.
highlights: The Palace of Sheki Khans, with shebeke lattice windows of 5,000 pieces each
The caravanserai, still taking guests

cities.name: Xınalıq
cities.why: A village at 2,300 metres whose people speak a language related to nothing else, reached by a single mountain road.
highlights: Flat-roofed stone houses stacked up the slope
The Ketsh language, spoken by a few thousand people and nobody else

cities.name: Brussels
cities.why: Art Nouveau streets, comic-strip walls, a gilded square, and the machinery of a continent in the eastern quarter.
highlights: The Grand-Place, best at night when it is lit and empty
Horta's houses, four of them UNESCO-listed

cities.name: Dinant
cities.why: A citadel on a cliff over the Meuse, a bulbous cathedral below, and the birthplace of the saxophone.
highlights: 408 steps or a cable car to the citadel
Kayaking the Lesse down to the river

cities.name: Antwerp
cities.why: Rubens's city and the world's diamond exchange, with a fashion school that reset the industry in the 1980s.
highlights: Rubens's own house and studio
The station, which is a cathedral pretending to be a station

cities.name: Bruges
cities.why: A trading city frozen when its river silted up in the 1500s, which is why it looks like this.
highlights: The belfry's 366 steps and the carillon at the top
Michelangelo's Madonna, the only sculpture he sold abroad in his lifetime

cities.name: Ghent
cities.why: Bruges's rival, larger, younger and still a working student city rather than a museum of itself.
highlights: The Ghent Altarpiece, restored, in the cathedral it was painted for
The Graslei quays at dusk

cities.name: Blagaj
cities.why: A dervish monastery built against a cliff at the source of the Buna, where a river comes out of a cave at full size.
highlights: The tekke, a Sufi lodge from around 1520, still in use
The spring, one of Europe's largest karst sources

cities.name: Mostar
cities.why: A 16th-century Ottoman bridge, destroyed in 1993 and rebuilt from the river stones, over a green-blue river.
highlights: Stari Most, and the divers who jump 24 metres from it
The old bazaar, at seven in the morning before the day trips

cities.name: Sarajevo
cities.why: An Ottoman bazaar at one end of a street and Habsburg apartment blocks at the other, in a valley ringed by mountains.
highlights: Baščaršija's coppersmiths, still hammering
The Tunnel of Hope, dug under the airport runway during the siege

cities.name: Travnik
cities.why: The Ottoman viziers' capital for 150 years, under a fortress, with a coloured mosque and a spring beneath it.
highlights: The Many-Coloured Mosque, painted rather than tiled
Ivo Andrić's birthplace, and the novel he set here

cities.name: Bansko
cities.why: A stone-built mountain town under Pirin, with cheap skiing in winter and hut-to-hut walking in summer.
highlights: Pirin national park's glacial lakes and the Vihren summit
Mehanas serving Bansko sausage and heavy red wine

cities.name: Rila Monastery
cities.why: A fortified monastery in a forested valley, founded in the 10th century, with striped arcades and frescoes over every surface.
highlights: The painted porch, with 1,200 scenes and no blank stone
Hrelyo's Tower, from 1335, the only medieval part left

cities.name: Sofia
cities.why: A capital with Roman ruins under the metro stations and a mountain at the end of the tram line.
highlights: Alexander Nevsky cathedral and its icon crypt
The Roman Serdica ruins, excavated and left open in the middle of the city

cities.name: Nessebar
cities.why: A rocky peninsula joined by a causeway, with more medieval churches per square metre than anywhere on the Black Sea.
highlights: Forty churches in a town of a few hundred metres across
Wooden Ottoman-era houses on stone bases

cities.name: Plovdiv
cities.why: One of Europe's oldest continuously inhabited cities, on six hills, with a Roman theatre still in use.
highlights: The Roman theatre, hosting opera and rock concerts since restoration
The Old Town's 19th-century merchant houses with overhanging upper floors

cities.name: Dubrovnik
cities.why: A maritime republic in near-perfect limestone, walled, car-free, and under real pressure from its own popularity.
highlights: The walls, walked at opening or in the last hour
Lokrum island, ten minutes by boat, with a monastery and peacocks

cities.name: Split
cities.why: A Roman emperor's retirement palace that became a town — people live inside the walls and always have.
highlights: Diocletian's Palace, occupied continuously since 305 AD
The Riva at passeggiata hour

cities.name: Vis
cities.why: The furthest inhabited Dalmatian island, closed to foreigners as a military base until 1989 and undeveloped because of it.
highlights: Stiniva cove, reached down a scree gully or by boat
Komiža's fishing harbour and the Blue Cave on Biševo

cities.name: Plitvice Lakes
cities.why: Sixteen terraced lakes falling into each other over travertine barriers that are still growing.
highlights: Boardwalks directly over the water — swimming is banned and enforced
The upper lakes, which most day visitors miss

cities.name: Zagreb
cities.why: A central European capital of coffee terraces and museums, with almost nothing Mediterranean about it.
highlights: The Museum of Broken Relationships, which is much better than the joke
Dolac market above the main square

cities.name: Motovun
cities.why: A walled hill town over a truffle forest, with a walkable rampart and a view of the whole Mirna valley.
highlights: Truffle hunting in the Motovun forest with dogs, October and November
The Parenzana, a disused railway turned cycle path

cities.name: Rovinj
cities.why: A Venetian fishing town on a former island, with a campanile copied from San Marco and houses straight into the sea.
highlights: The old town's stepped lanes, all of them ending at water
Golden Cape forest park, cycled or walked

cities.name: Nicosia
cities.why: A Venetian star-shaped fortress city with a UN buffer zone through the middle and a crossing on the main shopping street.
highlights: The Venetian walls, eleven bastions, still tracing the city
The Cyprus Museum's Neolithic and Bronze Age collections

cities.name: Paphos
cities.why: A harbour town with Roman villa floors that are among the finest mosaics anywhere, and royal tombs cut into the rock.
highlights: The House of Dionysos and its mosaic floors
Tombs of the Kings, Hellenistic and underground

cities.name: Omodos & the wine villages
cities.why: Cobbled mountain villages growing indigenous grapes nobody else has, around a 12th-century monastery.
highlights: Xynisteri and mavro, grape varieties grown almost nowhere else
The painted churches of the Troodos, ten of them UNESCO-listed

cities.name: Brno
cities.why: Czechia's second city: student, modernist and self-deprecating, with an ossuary of 50,000 under the square.
highlights: Villa Tugendhat, Mies van der Rohe, 1930, bookable in advance only
The second-largest ossuary in Europe, found in 2001

cities.name: Mikulov
cities.why: A chateau town on the Austrian border, surrounded by the country's best vineyards and a limestone ridge.
highlights: Wine cellars cut into the rock, open at harvest
The Jewish quarter and cemetery, one of central Europe's most important

cities.name: Český Krumlov
cities.why: A castle town in a tight loop of the Vltava, essentially unchanged since the 18th century.
highlights: The baroque theatre, with original 1766 machinery still working
The bear moat, which has had bears since the 1700s

cities.name: Český ráj (Turnov)
cities.why: 'Bohemian Paradise': sandstone towers, rock cities and castles on pinnacles, ninety minutes from Prague.
highlights: Prachovské skály's maze of rock corridors
Trosky castle on two volcanic plugs

cities.name: Prague
cities.why: Romanesque, gothic, baroque and cubist stacked on top of each other, with a castle above and a bridge in between.
highlights: Charles Bridge at six in the morning — genuinely worth the alarm
The castle complex and St Vitus's stained glass by Mucha

cities.name: Aarhus
cities.why: A student city with a rainbow walkway on its art museum and a reconstructed old town beneath it.
highlights: ARoS and Olafur Eliasson's circular rainbow panorama
Den Gamle By: 75 relocated buildings staged in three different decades

cities.name: Skagen
cities.why: The country's northern tip, where two seas meet visibly and a school of painters came for the light.
highlights: Grenen: stand with one foot in the Skagerrak and one in the Kattegat
The Skagen painters' museum and Anchers' house

cities.name: Copenhagen
cities.why: A harbour city clean enough to swim in the middle of, with the densest good eating in the Nordics.
highlights: Harbour baths at Islands Brygge — municipal swimming in the harbour
Designmuseum Danmark and the chairs everyone else copied

cities.name: Roskilde
cities.why: Viking ships raised from the fjord, thirty-nine Danish monarchs in one cathedral, and a festival in a field.
highlights: Five 11th-century ships, scuttled to block the fjord and dug out in 1962
The cathedral: Denmark's royal burial church since 1413

cities.name: Kuressaare, Saaremaa
cities.why: An island town around a moated bishop's castle, on Estonia's largest and slowest island.
highlights: The 14th-century castle, complete with its moat
Kaali meteorite crater, formed within human memory

cities.name: Tartu
cities.why: Estonia's intellectual capital since 1632, small, brick and argumentative.
highlights: The university's neoclassical main building and its student lock-up
Estonian National Museum, built on a Soviet runway

cities.name: Lahemaa
cities.why: A national park of bog, forest, manor houses and abandoned Soviet submarine bases, an hour east of the capital.
highlights: Viru bog boardwalk at dawn
Palmse and Sagadi manors, restored

cities.name: Tallinn
cities.why: A walled hanseatic town where the merchants' houses, the guild halls and the city wall all survived, and a startup district grew up beside them.
highlights: The intact town wall and twenty of its towers
Telliskivi's converted rail yards, where the country's design lives now

cities.name: Inari
cities.why: The centre of Sámi Finland, on a lake with three thousand islands.
highlights: Siida: the Sámi museum, written by Sámi people
Ukonsaari, a sacred island out on the lake

cities.name: Rovaniemi
cities.why: The gateway to Lapland, rebuilt after 1944 to an Alvar Aalto plan shaped like reindeer antlers.
highlights: Arktikum, the best museum on Arctic life anywhere
Husky and reindeer trails from December to March

cities.name: Helsinki
cities.why: Neoclassical centre, brutal-modern edges, and a design district you can walk in an afternoon.
highlights: Suomenlinna: a UNESCO sea fortress on six islands, twenty minutes by ferry
Temppeliaukio, a church blasted into bedrock

cities.name: Porvoo
cities.why: Red ochre warehouses on a river, and Finland's second-oldest town an hour from the capital.
highlights: The riverfront shore houses, painted for a royal visit in 1809
Cobbled old town with working chocolate and glass makers

cities.name: Savonlinna
cities.why: A 15th-century castle on an island in the middle of Saimaa, which hosts opera in its courtyard each July.
highlights: Olavinlinna castle, built to face east and never taken by storm
Opera in the courtyard, one month a year

cities.name: Annecy
cities.why: A canal town on the cleanest large lake in Europe, with the Alps standing straight up behind it.
highlights: Swimming in the lake from public beaches all summer
The 40 km lakeside cycle path on a former railway

cities.name: Beaune
cities.why: The wine capital of Burgundy, inside its own walls, on the most valuable agricultural land on earth.
highlights: The Hôtel-Dieu's glazed tile roof and 15th-century wards
Walking or cycling the Côte de Beaune between named vineyards

cities.name: Chamonix
cities.why: A valley town under the highest mountain in western Europe, where alpinism was invented.
highlights: Aiguille du Midi by cable car to 3,842 metres, in twenty minutes
The Mer de Glace, and the ladders marking where the ice used to be

cities.name: Colmar & the Alsace wine road
cities.why: Half-timbered, geranium-hung, and German four times in a century — the food and the wine still say so.
highlights: The Isenheim Altarpiece at the Unterlinden, which stops people mid-sentence
The wine road south through Eguisheim and Riquewihr

cities.name: Strasbourg
cities.why: A cathedral of pink sandstone over a half-timbered island, and the European Parliament twenty minutes away.
highlights: The cathedral's astronomical clock, which performs at half past twelve
La Petite France's canals and tanners' houses

cities.name: Clermont-Ferrand
cities.why: A city built in black volcanic stone under a chain of eighty dormant volcanoes.
highlights: The black lava cathedral, which looks like nothing else in France
Puy de Dôme, 1,465 metres, by rack railway or on foot

cities.name: Le Puy-en-Velay
cities.why: Chapels on top of volcanic plugs, green lentils with their own appellation, and the start of the oldest road to Santiago.
highlights: Saint-Michel d'Aiguilhe: 268 steps up a volcanic needle to a 10th-century chapel
The cathedral, and the pilgrim mass each morning before departure

cities.name: Amiens
cities.why: The largest gothic cathedral in France by volume, and market gardens on canals behind it.
highlights: The cathedral, twice the volume of Notre-Dame de Paris
Hortillonnages: 300 hectares of floating market gardens, seen from a punt

cities.name: Lille
cities.why: Flemish in its architecture and French in its administration, with the best food market north of Lyon.
highlights: Vieux Lille's Flemish brick and the Grand'Place
Palais des Beaux-Arts, the second-largest collection in France

cities.name: Reims
cities.why: Where thirty-three French kings were crowned, above twenty kilometres of Roman chalk cellars full of champagne.
highlights: The cathedral's smiling angel, and Chagall's windows behind the altar
Crayères: Gallo-Roman chalk pits, now cellars, at 10°C year-round

cities.name: Bonifacio
cities.why: A citadel on white limestone cliffs undercut by the sea, with Sardinia visible across twelve kilometres of strait.
highlights: The King of Aragon's staircase, 187 steps cut into the cliff face
Boat trips into the sea caves under the town

cities.name: Corte
cities.why: The old Corsican capital in the mountainous centre, with the university that keeps the language alive and the GR20 above it.
highlights: The citadel on a rock, and the museum of Corsica inside it
Restonica gorge, and the glacial lakes at the top of it

cities.name: Amboise & the Loire châteaux
cities.why: A royal town on the Loire, with Leonardo's last house at the top of it and Chenonceau downstream.
highlights: Chenonceau, built across the river itself
Clos Lucé, where Leonardo died in 1519

cities.name: Biarritz & the Basque Coast
cities.why: Atlantic surf, a Napoleonic resort, and a food culture that belongs to a nation without a state.
highlights: Surf at the Côte des Basques, where European surfing started in 1957
Pintxos across the border in San Sebastián, an hour away

cities.name: Bordeaux
cities.why: An 18th-century stone city on a river bend, cleaned in the 2000s, with the world's most famous vineyards at the gates.
highlights: The Place de la Bourse and its mirror of water
Saint-Émilion, a monolithic church cut into rock, forty minutes east

cities.name: La Rochelle
cities.why: A Protestant merchant port behind three medieval towers, with an island of white houses across a bridge.
highlights: The harbour towers, which held a chain across the entrance
Île de Ré: hollyhocks, salt marshes and 100 km of cycle path

cities.name: Sarlat & the Dordogne
cities.why: A honey-coloured medieval town in a valley of castles, walnut groves and the oldest painted caves in Europe.
highlights: Lascaux IV, an exact facsimile because the original is closed for its own survival
Castles facing each other across the river from the Hundred Years' War

cities.name: Toulouse
cities.why: The pink city: brick everything, a Romanesque basilica, aerospace money and a canal to the Mediterranean.
highlights: Saint-Sernin, the largest Romanesque church still standing
Canal du Midi, walked or cycled towards the sea

cities.name: Bayeux & the Landing Beaches
cities.why: A town that kept its cathedral, its 70-metre embroidery of 1066, and the beaches of 1944 twenty minutes away.
highlights: The Bayeux Tapestry, seen slowly with the audio guide
Omaha and the American cemetery above it

cities.name: Mont-Saint-Michel
cities.why: An abbey on a rock in a bay with the fastest tides in Europe, and a village winding up to it.
highlights: The abbey at opening or on a night visit, not at noon
Walking the bay barefoot with a guide, which is the only safe way

cities.name: Saint-Malo
cities.why: A corsair city inside granite ramparts, rebuilt stone by stone after 1944, with a tidal range of twelve metres.
highlights: The ramparts circuit at high tide, when spray comes over
Walking to the Grand Bé island at low water — and watching the clock

cities.name: Chartres
cities.why: The most complete Gothic cathedral in France, with 172 windows of 12th-century glass that survived two wars in boxes.
highlights: The blue of the Notre-Dame de la Belle-Verrière window
The labyrinth in the nave floor, walkable on Fridays in summer

cities.name: Paris
cities.why: Nineteenth-century town planning at monumental scale, with the world's densest concentration of art inside it.
highlights: The Musée d'Orsay in a railway station, better than the Louvre for a single visit
Père Lachaise, a walled city of the dead with its own map

cities.name: Arles
cities.why: A Roman arena still in use, the Rhône delta at the door, and the year Van Gogh painted two hundred canvases here.
highlights: The amphitheatre, built in 90 AD and still hosting events
The Camargue: salt, white horses, flamingos, and a rice crop

cities.name: Avignon
cities.why: Seven popes ruled from here in the 14th century and left the largest gothic palace in the world behind them.
highlights: The Palais des Papes, more fortress than palace
The famous half-bridge, which stops in the Rhône

cities.name: Carcassonne
cities.why: A double-walled citadel of 52 towers, heavily restored in the 1850s and argued about ever since.
highlights: The walls at night, when the day visitors have gone and it is floodlit
Viollet-le-Duc's restoration, and the debate about whether it invented as much as it saved

cities.name: Marseille
cities.why: France's oldest city, founded by Greeks in 600 BC, Mediterranean rather than French in almost every respect.
highlights: The Calanques: white limestone inlets, reachable on foot from the edge of town
MuCEM and the footbridge to the fort

cities.name: Nice
cities.why: An Italian city until 1860, with an old town that still cooks like one and a pebble bay that never closes.
highlights: The Cours Saleya market, and socca eaten standing up
Matisse and Chagall museums up the hill in Cimiez

cities.name: Sighnaghi & Kakheti
cities.why: A walled hill town over the Alazani valley, with the Caucasus on the horizon and vineyards to the foot of them.
highlights: Family cellars fermenting in buried qvevri
The town walls, 4 km with 23 towers

cities.name: Tbilisi
cities.why: Wooden balconies, a fortress above, sulphur baths below, and Persian, Russian and Soviet layers in the same street.
highlights: The sulphur bath district, with domed brick roofs at ground level
Narikala fortress and the cable car to it

cities.name: Stepantsminda (Kazbegi)
cities.why: A village under a 5,047-metre volcano, with a 14th-century church on a spur above it.
highlights: Gergeti Trinity church, walked up in two hours
The Georgian Military Highway through the Jvari pass

cities.name: Mestia, Svaneti
cities.why: A mountain region of defensive stone towers built by families against each other, under 5,000-metre peaks.
highlights: Koshki towers, 9th to 13th century, one per family
Ushguli, among the highest permanently inhabited villages in Europe

cities.name: Berchtesgaden
cities.why: An alpine corner surrounded on three sides by Austria, with a fjord-green lake below the Watzmann.
highlights: Königssee, crossed by electric boats since 1909 so the echo carries
The salt mine, worked since 1517, entered on a wooden slide

cities.name: Munich
cities.why: A wealthy southern capital with the Alps an hour away and a river you can surf in the middle of a park.
highlights: The Eisbach standing wave, surfed year-round in the English Garden
The Alte Pinakothek's Rubens and Dürer

cities.name: Berlin
cities.why: Poor, sexy, enormous and unfinished — five museums on one island and a wall memorial that refuses to be comfortable.
highlights: Museum Island, especially the Pergamon's scale and the Neues Museum's Nefertiti
The Berlin Wall Memorial at Bernauer Straße — the honest one, not Checkpoint Charlie

cities.name: Dresden
cities.why: A baroque royal capital burned in 1945 and rebuilt stone by numbered stone, on a river bend.
highlights: The Frauenkirche, reassembled from the rubble and finished in 2005
The Green Vault's treasury, booked in timed slots

cities.name: Leipzig
cities.why: Bach's church, a peaceful revolution that started in it, and a cotton mill full of painters.
highlights: Bach's Thomaskirche, where he was cantor for 27 years
The Nikolaikirche and the Monday demonstrations of 1989

cities.name: Hamburg
cities.why: A merchant republic and Europe's third port, with more bridges than Venice and Amsterdam together.
highlights: The Elbphilharmonie, and its free public plaza at 37 metres
Speicherstadt's brick warehouse city on oak piles

cities.name: Lübeck
cities.why: The queen of the Hanseatic League, on an island, in brick gothic, and the home of marzipan.
highlights: The Holstentor, leaning and famous and on the old fifty-mark note
Seven towers on the island skyline

cities.name: Bacharach & the Rhine Gorge
cities.why: Half-timbered wine village under a ruined chapel, in the 65-kilometre UNESCO stretch of castles.
highlights: Forty castles in sixty-five kilometres of river
Riesling from slate slopes at 60 degrees

cities.name: Cologne
cities.why: A Roman city with a Gothic cathedral that took 632 years and dominates everything.
highlights: The Dom, and 533 steps up the south tower
Kölsch served in 200 ml glasses, replaced until you cover it with the mat

cities.name: Athens
cities.why: A sprawling modern capital with a 2,500-year-old temple on a rock in the middle and a food scene that got very good, quietly.
highlights: The Acropolis at opening, and the Acropolis Museum afterwards, in that order
The National Archaeological Museum, which is the real prize

cities.name: Delphi
cities.why: The navel of the ancient world, on a terrace of Mount Parnassus above a sea of olive trees.
highlights: The sacred way up to the temple of Apollo, where the oracle spoke
The bronze Charioteer, which survived because an earthquake buried it

cities.name: Hydra
cities.why: An island two hours from Athens with no cars and no bicycles at all — mules, boats and feet.
highlights: Shipowners' mansions round a stone harbour, from the 1790s
No wheeled traffic of any kind, by law

cities.name: Kardamyli & the Mani
cities.why: Stone tower houses on a wild peninsula where blood feuds ran into the 20th century, above a clear sea.
highlights: Tower villages built for feuding families, still standing empty
The Viros gorge, walked from the sea up into Taygetos

cities.name: Monemvasia
cities.why: A Byzantine town hidden on the seaward side of a rock island, invisible from the mainland.
highlights: A single gate, and no cars inside the walls
The upper town's ruins and Hagia Sophia on the summit

cities.name: Mystras
cities.why: A Byzantine city on a spur of Taygetos, abandoned in the 1950s and left standing: palaces, churches and frescoes.
highlights: A whole late-Byzantine city, walked from the castle down
Frescoes in six churches, most of them unrestored

cities.name: Nafplio
cities.why: Greece's first capital: Venetian, neoclassical, under two fortresses, on a gulf in the Peloponnese.
highlights: Palamidi fortress and its 999 steps
Epidaurus's theatre, where a coin dropped on stage is audible in the back row

cities.name: Olympia
cities.why: Where the games were held every four years for a millennium, in a wooded valley between two rivers.
highlights: The original stadium, entered through its vaulted tunnel
The workshop of Pheidias, identified by a cup with his name on it

cities.name: Ioannina
cities.why: An Ottoman lake city with an island in it, a silversmithing tradition and the gateway to Zagori.
highlights: The walled kastro, and two mosques still standing inside it
The island, reached in ten minutes, with five monasteries and no cars

cities.name: Kavala
cities.why: An Ottoman aqueduct over a harbour town, with Philippi's ruins inland and Thasos across the water.
highlights: The Kamares aqueduct, striding across the middle of town
Philippi: a Roman city, a battlefield, and where Paul first preached in Europe

cities.name: Meteora (Kalambaka)
cities.why: Six working monasteries on top of sandstone pillars, reached for centuries by rope ladder and net.
highlights: The footpaths between monasteries, which almost every visitor drives instead
Frescoes inside Varlaam and Great Meteoron

cities.name: Pelion (Makrinitsa)
cities.why: Stone villages with slate roofs on a wooded mountain that drops to beaches on both sides.
highlights: Kalderimia: cobbled mule paths between villages, still the best way around
The narrow-gauge Moutzouris railway, built by Evaristo de Chirico

cities.name: Thessaloniki
cities.why: Greece's second city: Byzantine, Ottoman and Sephardic layers, and the country's most confident food.
highlights: The Rotunda and the Byzantine churches on the UNESCO list
Modiano and Kapani markets, then bougatsa for breakfast

cities.name: Zagori (Monodendri)
cities.why: Forty-six stone villages in the Pindus mountains, linked by packhorse bridges over the deepest gorge in the world by ratio.
highlights: The Vikos gorge, from the Oxya viewpoint or from inside it
Arched stone bridges built by 18th-century merchant guilds

cities.name: Chania, Crete
cities.why: A Venetian harbour with an Ottoman quarter behind it, on an island large enough to be its own country.
highlights: The Venetian lighthouse and the harbour arc
Samaria gorge: 16 km down through the White Mountains to the sea

cities.name: Corfu
cities.why: Venetian for four centuries and British for fifty, green all year, with an old town that looks nothing like the Aegean.
highlights: The UNESCO old town, Venetian streets and two fortresses
Cricket on the Spianada, a British hangover

cities.name: Heraklion & Knossos
cities.why: Crete's capital and the Minoan palace beside it — Europe's oldest city, and a reconstruction people still argue about.
highlights: Knossos, and Evans's concrete reconstructions, which are the argument
The archaeological museum, which holds what Knossos actually yielded

cities.name: Ikaria
cities.why: A steep island where people routinely live past ninety, festivals start at midnight and shops open when they open.
highlights: Panigiria: village festivals that run until dawn and are not for tourists
Radioactive hot springs at Therma, used since antiquity

cities.name: Kefalonia
cities.why: The largest Ionian island: an underground lake, a mountain of black fir, and the loggerhead turtles offshore.
highlights: Melissani cave, where the roof collapsed and the light comes straight down
Mount Ainos, black fir found nowhere else

cities.name: Milos
cities.why: A volcanic island of white rock formations, coloured mining beaches and boat-only coves.
highlights: Sarakiniko: white pumice worn into a moonscape by the sea
Kleftiko's sea caves, reachable only by boat

cities.name: Naxos
cities.why: The largest Cycladic island: mountain villages, marble quarries, a working agricultural interior and long sandy beaches.
highlights: The Portara, a temple doorway on an islet at the harbour
Halki and the mountain villages, with citron distilleries

cities.name: Paros
cities.why: Cycladic in the way people imagine the Cyclades, with marble quarries that supplied the ancient world and a working town behind the beaches.
highlights: Naoussa's small harbour, before the evening crowd
The Byzantine road, a marble path over the hills to Lefkes

cities.name: Rhodes
cities.why: A walled medieval city built by crusader knights, on an island of Ottoman villages and butterfly valleys.
highlights: The largest inhabited medieval town in Europe, inside four kilometres of wall
Lindos's acropolis above a white village and a bay

cities.name: Santorini
cities.why: The rim of a drowned volcano, with villages on the edge of a 300-metre cliff and vines grown in baskets on the ground.
highlights: Akrotiri: a Bronze Age town buried in ash and preserved whole
Assyrtiko from vines trained into wreaths against the wind

cities.name: Symi
cities.why: Neoclassical mansions in ochre and blue stacked round a horseshoe harbour, an hour from Rhodes.
highlights: The harbour at Gialos, which is the reason to come
Panormitis monastery at the southern end, reached by boat

cities.name: Tihany, Lake Balaton
cities.why: A lavender peninsula with an abbey on a cliff, sticking into a shallow warm lake.
highlights: The abbey and its 1055 founding charter — the oldest written Hungarian
Lavender fields in late June

cities.name: Tokaj
cities.why: The world's first classified wine region, from 1737, on volcanic slopes at a river confluence.
highlights: Aszú berries picked individually, one shrivelled grape at a time
Cellars cut into rock and furred with black mould

cities.name: Budapest
cities.why: Hilly Buda and flat Pest, joined by bridges, with a parliament on the water and a hundred hot springs underneath.
highlights: Széchenyi and Gellért baths — one grand and outdoor, one Art Nouveau and indoor
The parliament, seen from the Buda side at night

cities.name: Szentendre
cities.why: A Serbian Orthodox artists' town on the river, forty minutes from the capital by suburban rail.
highlights: Orthodox churches from the 18th-century Serb migration
The open-air ethnographic museum outside town

cities.name: Reykjavík
cities.why: The northernmost capital of a sovereign state, small enough to cross on foot and loud on Friday nights.
highlights: Hallgrímskirkja's basalt-column tower, and the view from the top
The Settlement Exhibition, built around a 10th-century longhouse found under the street

cities.name: Þingvellir
cities.why: A rift valley where the Atlantic plates pull apart, and where Iceland's parliament met in the open air from 930.
highlights: Walk the Almannagjá fissure between two continents
The Law Rock, where the Althing was proclaimed for eight centuries

cities.name: Höfn & Jökulsárlón
cities.why: A langoustine port beside Europe's largest ice cap, where icebergs float out to sea past a car park.
highlights: Jökulsárlón lagoon and the Diamond Beach opposite
Vatnajökull: 8% of the country, under ice

cities.name: Vík í Mýrdal
cities.why: A village of three hundred under a glacier, with black sand and dangerous surf.
highlights: Reynisfjara's basalt columns — and the sneaker waves that kill people who turn their backs
Dyrhólaey's arch and puffin colony in early summer

cities.name: Húsavík
cities.why: A wooden church, a whale museum, and the most reliable whale watching in Europe.
highlights: Humpbacks in Skjálfandi bay, April to October
The whale museum, built by the people who stopped hunting them

cities.name: Ísafjörður
cities.why: The Westfjords' capital: 2,700 people at the end of a fjord under a flat-topped mountain.
highlights: Hornstrandir, a roadless nature reserve reached by boat
Dynjandi, the waterfall that falls in seven tiers

cities.name: Dublin
cities.why: Georgian squares, a 1,200-year-old river crossing, and four Nobel laureates in literature from one small city.
highlights: The Book of Kells and the Long Room at Trinity
Kilmainham Gaol, where the 1916 leaders were executed

cities.name: Glendalough
cities.why: A 6th-century monastic city in a glacial valley with two lakes, an hour from Dublin.
highlights: The round tower, 30 metres, built as a bell tower and a refuge
The Spinc ridge walk above the upper lake

cities.name: The Aran Islands (Inis Mór)
cities.why: Three limestone islands where Irish is the daily language and stone walls divide fields the size of rooms.
highlights: Dún Aonghasa, a prehistoric fort on an 87-metre cliff with no railing
1,600 km of dry stone wall on an island 14 km long

cities.name: Dingle
cities.why: A fishing town on a peninsula of beehive huts, empty beaches and the westernmost point of Europe's mainland fringe.
highlights: The Slea Head drive, and stopping at the clocháin
Gallarus Oratory, dry-stone and watertight after 1,200 years

cities.name: Galway
cities.why: A small port city that plays music every night of the week and treats a festival as its natural state.
highlights: Music in the Latin Quarter, from about nine
Oysters and Guinness at a bar that shucks them in front of you

cities.name: Bellagio & Lake Como
cities.why: A village on the point where the lake divides, with villa gardens on both arms and ferries between them.
highlights: Villa Melzi and Villa Carlotta's gardens, best in May for the azaleas
The car ferry across to Varenna and Menaggio, used as transport

cities.name: Milan
cities.why: Italy's working city: fashion, design, finance, and a Last Supper that has to be booked months ahead.
highlights: The Duomo roof terraces, walked among the spires
Leonardo's Last Supper, fifteen minutes, booked in advance

cities.name: Ortisei & the Dolomites
cities.why: Pale limestone towers over alpine meadows, in a valley where Ladin is still the first language.
highlights: Alpe di Siusi, the largest high-altitude meadow in Europe
Via ferrata routes built by soldiers in 1915–18

cities.name: Trieste
cities.why: Austro-Hungarian, Italian, Slovene and Jewish at once, on a limestone edge above the Adriatic, with the best coffee culture in Italy.
highlights: Piazza Unità d'Italia, the largest sea-facing square in Europe
The Risiera di San Sabba, the only Nazi camp with a crematorium on Italian soil

cities.name: Turin
cities.why: The first capital of Italy: baroque arcades, an Egyptian museum second only to Cairo's, and vermouth invented in a bar here.
highlights: The Museo Egizio, which has more than most Egyptian cities
Eighteen kilometres of arcades, so the court could walk in the rain

cities.name: Venice
cities.why: A city on wooden piles in a lagoon, with no roads, fewer than 50,000 residents left, and no equivalent anywhere.
highlights: Cannaregio and Castello, where people still live
The Accademia and the Punta della Dogana at opposite ends of taste

cities.name: Vernazza & the Cinque Terre
cities.why: Five fishing villages on a cliff coast, joined by terraced footpaths and a railway in a tunnel.
highlights: The Sentiero Azzurro between villages, ticketed and sometimes closed by landslip
Dry-stone terraces holding the vineyards up — 6,700 km of wall in total

cities.name: Verona
cities.why: A Roman arena still used for opera, a river bend of pink marble streets, and Valpolicella in the hills above.
highlights: Opera in the 1st-century arena, on cushions, in summer
San Zeno's bronze doors and Mantegna altarpiece

cities.name: Civita di Bagnoregio
cities.why: A village on an eroding tufa pillar, reached by a footbridge, with about a dozen permanent residents left.
highlights: The bridge, which is the only way in and takes ten minutes
Etruscan tunnels cut under the rock

cities.name: Orvieto
cities.why: A town on a plug of volcanic rock with a striped cathedral and an Etruscan city tunnelled underneath it.
highlights: The cathedral facade, and Signorelli's apocalypse frescoes inside
St Patrick's Well: a double-helix staircase 54 metres down

cities.name: Rome
cities.why: A city where an insurance office sits on a temple and nobody comments, with the best street-level food in Italy.
highlights: The Pantheon, entered free, still roofed by the largest unreinforced concrete dome ever built
The Forum and Palatine early, before the heat and the groups

cities.name: Alghero, Sardinia
cities.why: A Catalan-speaking walled port on Sardinia's northwest coast, with sea caves and Bronze Age towers inland.
highlights: Catalan street signs, and a dialect spoken since the 14th century
Neptune's Grotto, reached by 654 steps down a cliff

cities.name: Lecce
cities.why: Baroque carved in soft golden limestone, in the heel of Italy, an hour from two seas.
highlights: Santa Croce's facade, which took a century and shows it
A Roman amphitheatre found under the main square in 1901

cities.name: Lipari & the Aeolians
cities.why: Seven volcanic islands off Sicily, one of them erupting every twenty minutes, all of them on the UNESCO list.
highlights: Stromboli's explosions, watched from a boat at dusk
Pumice and obsidian quarries on Lipari, white against black

cities.name: Matera
cities.why: Cave dwellings inhabited for nine thousand years, evacuated in 1952 as a national disgrace, now a UNESCO site.
highlights: The Sassi, and rock churches with Byzantine frescoes
A restored cave house showing how families and animals shared one room

cities.name: Naples
cities.why: Loud, dense, Greek in origin, with the best pizza and the best archaeological museum in the world.
highlights: The Archaeological Museum, which holds everything good from Pompeii
Pizza in a room with a wood oven and four tables

cities.name: Palermo
cities.why: Norman, Arab and Byzantine in the same building, with the best street food in Italy underneath.
highlights: The Cappella Palatina: Islamic ceiling, Byzantine mosaics, Norman king
Ballarò and Capo markets, shouted rather than sold

cities.name: Syracuse & Ortigia
cities.why: Once the most powerful Greek city in the world, now an island old town with a Doric temple inside the cathedral.
highlights: The cathedral, built inside a 5th-century BC temple, columns and all
The Greek theatre, still used for classical drama each summer

cities.name: Arezzo
cities.why: A hill town with Piero della Francesca's greatest fresco cycle and none of Florence's queue.
highlights: The Legend of the True Cross in San Francesco, booked in slots of twenty-five
The sloping Piazza Grande, and the joust held on it twice a year

cities.name: Bologna
cities.why: Forty kilometres of porticoes, the oldest university in the world, and the best eating in Italy.
highlights: The Quadrilatero's food shops, unchanged in layout since the Middle Ages
Portico di San Luca: 666 arches uphill to a basilica

cities.name: Florence
cities.why: A banking city that funded the Renaissance and kept nearly all of it inside a twenty-minute walk.
highlights: Brunelleschi's dome, climbed at opening
The Uffizi, booked, and the Bargello, which is empty and holds the sculpture

cities.name: Lucca
cities.why: An intact Renaissance wall, four kilometres round, wide enough on top to be a park, with a Roman amphitheatre turned into a square inside it.
highlights: Cycling the walls, which is what the whole city does at six
Piazza dell'Anfiteatro: the amphitheatre's oval, built over in houses

cities.name: Siena
cities.why: A medieval city that lost to Florence and was preserved by losing, arranged around a shell-shaped square.
highlights: The Campo, and the Palio run around it twice each summer
The cathedral's inlaid marble floor, uncovered a few weeks a year

cities.name: Assisi
cities.why: A pink stone town on Monte Subasio, built around the basilica of a man who rejected everything it is made of.
highlights: Giotto's fresco cycle in the upper basilica, restored after the 1997 earthquake
The Eremo delle Carceri, the hermitage in the woods above town

cities.name: Urbino
cities.why: A hilltop ducal palace that was the model Renaissance court, in a town that has been a university since 1506.
highlights: Piero della Francesca's Flagellation, a small painting people travel for
The duke's studiolo, panelled in trompe-l'œil marquetry

cities.name: Pristina
cities.why: A capital of cafés, brutalist landmarks and a median age under thirty.
highlights: The National Library, which everyone has an opinion about
Newborn, the typographic monument repainted every year

cities.name: Peja & Rugova
cities.why: A bazaar town at the mouth of a limestone gorge, with a patriarchate monastery and the Accursed Mountains behind.
highlights: The Patriarchate of Peć, a UNESCO site and the seat of the Serbian church
Rugova canyon, and via ferrata routes in it

cities.name: Prizren
cities.why: A river town of mosques, Orthodox churches and a stone bridge, under a fortress with the whole valley below it.
highlights: Sinan Pasha mosque and the Church of Our Lady of Ljeviš, on the same street
The fortress at sunset, walked up in twenty minutes

cities.name: Kuldīga
cities.why: A wooden town on Europe's widest waterfall, which is only two metres high but 249 metres across.
highlights: Ventas rumba, where fish jump the falls in spring
Latvia's longest brick bridge, from 1874

cities.name: Liepāja
cities.why: A wind-blown port with a derelict tsarist naval town at its northern end and a rock music habit.
highlights: Karosta: a Russian imperial naval base, half-ruined, still lived in
The northern forts collapsing into the sea

cities.name: Riga
cities.why: A hanseatic old town wrapped in a boulevard ring, wrapped in the best Art Nouveau streets in Europe.
highlights: Alberta iela, where Mikhail Eisenstein put faces on every facade
The Central Market in five Zeppelin hangars

cities.name: Sigulda
cities.why: Three castles above a sandstone river gorge, an hour from Riga by train.
highlights: Turaida's red brick castle above the Gauja
Gūtmanis cave, carved with visitors' names since the 1600s

cities.name: Malbun
cities.why: The country's only ski area, in a high bowl at 1,600 metres, with marmots and a chairlift.
highlights: The Fürstensteig, a wired cliff path with real exposure
Small, cheap, uncrowded skiing in winter

cities.name: Vaduz
cities.why: A capital of 5,700 people under a castle the prince actually lives in, with a black concrete art museum on the main street.
highlights: Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein and the princely collections
The vineyard walk below the castle

cities.name: Nida, Curonian Spit
cities.why: Wooden fishermen's houses under a moving dune, on a sand spit between lagoon and sea.
highlights: Parnidis dune and its sundial, with the Russian border visible south
Thomas Mann's summer house, where he wrote in 1930–32

cities.name: Šiauliai
cities.why: An industrial town whose reason to visit stands in a field twelve kilometres north.
highlights: The Hill of Crosses: over 100,000 crosses, bulldozed three times by the Soviets and rebuilt each night
The sound the small crosses make in wind

cities.name: Trakai
cities.why: A red brick island castle in a lake, and the Karaim community that has lived beside it since the 14th century.
highlights: The island castle, reachable by footbridge
Kibinai pastries in Karaim wooden houses

cities.name: Vilnius
cities.why: Forty churches, endless courtyards, and a self-declared republic of artists over the river.
highlights: St Anne's, which Napoleon reportedly wanted to carry to Paris
The Gate of Dawn and its silver icon, still a pilgrimage

cities.name: Luxembourg City
cities.why: A UNESCO-listed fortress on cliffs, with 17 kilometres of tunnels underneath and a modern quarter on the plateau above.
highlights: The Bock casemates, cut into the rock from 1644
The Chemin de la Corniche, called Europe's most beautiful balcony

cities.name: Remich & the Moselle
cities.why: Terraced vineyards on a slow river, with Germany on the far bank and Crémant cellars on this one.
highlights: Crémant tasting where it is bottled
The riverside cycle path along both banks

cities.name: Echternach
cities.why: The country's oldest town, with a 7th-century abbey and a hopping procession on the UNESCO list.
highlights: The Mullerthal Trail through sandstone clefts and moss
The basilica and its crypt

cities.name: Vianden
cities.why: A restored hilltop castle above a river village, where Victor Hugo spent his exile.
highlights: The castle, one of the largest west of the Rhine
Hugo's house on the bridge, kept as it was

cities.name: Victoria, Gozo
cities.why: A citadel town in the middle of an island where the pace drops noticeably the moment the ferry docks.
highlights: The Ċittadella walls, and the whole island visible from them
Ġgantija: temples older than Ħaġar Qim, and older than the pyramids

cities.name: Ħaġar Qim & the South Cliffs
cities.why: Megalithic temples on a cliff over the sea, built between 3600 and 3200 BC.
highlights: Some of the oldest free-standing structures on earth
The solstice alignment through a small oval port

cities.name: Mdina & Rabat
cities.why: The old walled capital on a hill, with about 250 residents and no traffic — called the silent city for a reason.
highlights: The bastion walls over the whole island at dusk
St Paul's catacombs, cut in the 3rd century

cities.name: Valletta
cities.why: A planned fortress city of 1566, on a peninsula between two harbours, with Caravaggio's largest painting in its cathedral.
highlights: St John's Co-Cathedral, plain outside and overwhelming inside
Caravaggio's Beheading of St John, the only work he signed

cities.name: Chișinău
cities.why: A green, low-rise capital of parks and Soviet-era planning, with the wine country immediately outside it.
highlights: Cricova and Mileștii Mici, driven through by car
The central market, and the produce of a country that mostly farms

cities.name: Orheiul Vechi
cities.why: A monastery dug into a limestone cliff over a loop of the Răut, inhabited on and off since the 13th century.
highlights: The cave church, reached along the cliff edge
Butuceni village below, with guesthouses in stone houses

cities.name: Monaco-Ville
cities.why: The medieval quarter on the rock: palace, cathedral, and an oceanographic museum built into the cliff face.
highlights: The Oceanographic Museum, founded by a prince who was a serious scientist
The changing of the guard at 11:55, briskly

cities.name: Kotor
cities.region: The Bay of Kotor & the Coast
cities.why: A walled Venetian town at the head of the bay, with fortifications climbing 260 metres up the cliff behind it.
highlights: The 1,350 steps up the fortress walls, at dawn before the heat
The old town's cats, which have their own museum

cities.name: Perast
cities.region: The Bay of Kotor & the Coast
cities.why: One street, sixteen baroque palaces, two islands offshore, and no room for a car.
highlights: The boat to Our Lady of the Rocks, five minutes offshore
Palaces built by sea captains who served Venice

cities.name: Žabljak
cities.why: The highest town in the Balkans at 1,450 metres, at the edge of Durmitor national park.
highlights: The Black Lake, twenty minutes' walk from the town
Bobotov Kuk, 2,523 metres, a long day on rock

cities.name: Texel
cities.why: The largest Wadden island: dunes, sheep, seals and thirty kilometres of empty North Sea beach.
highlights: Seal colonies on the sandbanks, seen from a boat
Bird reserves on the migration route, best in spring

cities.name: Amsterdam
cities.why: A 17th-century canal plan that still works, with two of the world's great collections inside it.
highlights: The Rijksmuseum, and half an hour in front of the Vermeers
The Van Gogh Museum, booked ahead or not at all

cities.name: Rotterdam
cities.why: Flattened in 1940 and rebuilt as an argument for modern architecture, on Europe's largest port.
highlights: The Markthal, a food market inside a housing block
Depot Boijmans, the first publicly accessible art storage building anywhere

cities.name: Utrecht
cities.why: Amsterdam's canals at half the scale and a fifth of the crowd, with wharf cellars at water level.
highlights: The Oudegracht's two-level canals, unique in Europe
The Dom tower, 112 metres, 465 steps

cities.name: Bitola
cities.why: A former consular city with a wide pedestrian avenue, and the Roman ruins of Heraclea on its edge.
highlights: Širok Sokak, built for nineteenth-century diplomats and still promenaded
Heraclea Lyncestis's mosaic floors

cities.name: Ohrid
cities.why: A town of Byzantine churches on a cliff over one of the world's oldest lakes, with a Slavic literary tradition that began here.
highlights: Sveti Jovan Kaneo, on a cliff over the water
The lake itself: 3–5 million years old, 288 metres deep

cities.name: Skopje
cities.why: A capital with the largest Ottoman bazaar in the Balkans on one bank and a marble-clad neoclassical rebuild on the other.
highlights: The Old Bazaar, trading continuously since the 12th century
The Stone Bridge, and the argument in stone on either side of it

cities.name: Ålesund
cities.why: Burned to the ground in 1904 and rebuilt, all at once, in Art Nouveau — so the whole town matches.
highlights: 418 steps up Aksla for the archipelago laid out below
The Jugendstil centre, in the old pharmacy

cities.name: Balestrand
cities.why: A Sognefjord village of dragon-style timber villas, where 19th-century painters came and then stayed.
highlights: Dragestil villas, a Norwegian national-romantic invention
The English church of St Olaf, built by a homesick Englishwoman in 1897

cities.name: Bergen
cities.why: A hanseatic trading port wedged between seven mountains, wet 200 days a year and entirely unbothered about it.
highlights: Bryggen's leaning wooden warehouses, and the fire history that explains their gaps
The Fløibanen funicular to a mountain you can walk down in an hour

cities.name: Flåm
cities.why: A hamlet at the end of a fjord arm, famous for a railway that drops 865 metres in twenty kilometres.
highlights: The Flåm Railway, best taken uphill and walked or cycled back down
Nærøyfjord: a UNESCO-listed fjord arm 250 metres wide at its narrowest

cities.name: Geiranger
cities.why: A UNESCO fjord arm 15 km long with waterfalls falling straight into it and abandoned farms on ledges above.
highlights: The Seven Sisters falls, and the farm ruins on shelves opposite
Dalsnibba, 1,500 metres, with the fjord directly below

cities.name: Odda & Trolltunga
cities.why: A smelter town at the end of a fjord arm, and a slab of rock that sticks 700 metres out over a lake.
highlights: Trolltunga: 28 km round, ten hours, and not a stroll
Folgefonna glacier above the valley

cities.name: Stavanger
cities.why: Oil capital with a preserved wooden old town, and the most photographed cliff in Norway an hour away.
highlights: Gamle Stavanger: 173 white wooden houses from the 18th century
Preikestolen, a 604-metre flat cliff, four hours there and back

cities.name: Voss
cities.why: A lake town between two fjords that decided to become Norway's outdoor sports capital and succeeded.
highlights: Skydiving, paragliding and rafting, all within the town
The Bergen Railway stops here, which is how everyone arrives

cities.name: Alta
cities.why: Finnmark's largest town, with 6,000-year-old rock carvings and a cathedral shaped like the aurora.
highlights: Hjemmeluft's rock art, on the UNESCO list, walked on boardwalks
The Northern Lights Cathedral, a titanium spiral

cities.name: Bodø
cities.why: A rebuilt northern port with the strongest tidal current in the world at its door and Lofoten across the water.
highlights: Saltstraumen: 400 million cubic metres of water through a 150-metre strait, four times a day
The coastal ferry and the Lofoten crossing

cities.name: Lofoten (Svolvær)
cities.why: Granite peaks that rise straight from the sea, red fishermen's cabins below them, and cod drying on racks every spring.
highlights: Reine and Hamnøy, the two views that put Lofoten on every screen
Ryten and Reinebringen — short, steep, and worth the calves

cities.name: Narvik
cities.why: An ice-free ore port at the end of a Swedish railway, ringed by mountains that drop into the fjord.
highlights: The Ofoten Railway to Kiruna, built for iron ore in 1902
The war museum, on a town fought over for two months in 1940

cities.name: Nordkapp (Honningsvåg)
cities.why: A cliff at 71°N sold as the top of Europe, on an island reached by tunnel, with a fishing town below it.
highlights: The plateau at midnight in June, with the sun still up
Gjesvær's bird cliffs: puffins, gannets and 100,000 pairs

cities.name: Senja
cities.why: Norway's second-largest island — Lofoten's landscape without Lofoten's traffic, and almost no one on the trails.
highlights: Segla and Hesten: short, steep, and among the best views in the country
Fishing villages on the outer coast with working boats

cities.name: Tromsø
cities.why: A university town at 69°N with more bars per head than anywhere else in Norway, and the aurora directly overhead.
highlights: The Arctic Cathedral and the cable car above the strait
Aurora hunting between late September and late March, inland where the sky is clearer

cities.name: Fredrikstad
cities.why: Scandinavia's best-preserved fortress town, on an island in a river mouth, reached by a free ferry.
highlights: Gamlebyen: ramparts, moat and cobbles, still inhabited
The free city ferry, which is public transport and runs all day

cities.name: Lillehammer
cities.why: Olympic town on a long lake, with an open-air museum that is really a village of 200 relocated buildings.
highlights: Maihaugen: farms, a stave church and a whole timber town, walked rather than viewed
The 1994 Olympic bob track, still rideable

cities.name: Oslo
cities.why: A capital that spent its oil money on architecture and then put a forest and a fjord within a tram ride of the result.
highlights: The Munch museum and the National Museum, which between them hold the versions of The Scream worth arguing about
The Fram and Kon-Tiki polar ships, kept whole in Bygdøy

cities.name: Rjukan
cities.why: A company town in a gorge so deep the sun does not reach it for six months, so the town installed mirrors on the mountain.
highlights: The sun mirrors on Gvepseborg, throwing daylight into the square since 2013
Vemork: the heavy water plant sabotaged in 1943, now a museum

cities.name: Kristiansand
cities.why: A grid-planned town on the warmest stretch of Norwegian coast, with a bathing park in the middle of it.
highlights: Posebyen's white timber quarter, 200 years of it
Bystranda, a city beach that is genuinely used

cities.name: Lindesnes
cities.why: Norway's southernmost point, with a lighthouse on it and a restaurant five metres under the sea beside it.
highlights: The lighthouse, lit since 1656
Under: a dining room submerged against the seabed

cities.name: Risør
cities.why: 'The white town by the Skagerrak' — 300 wooden houses round a harbour, and a wooden boat festival each August.
highlights: The wooden boat festival, the largest in the Nordics
Stangholmen lighthouse island, twenty minutes by boat

cities.name: Longyearbyen
cities.why: The world's northernmost town of any size: a coal settlement turned research station, where leaving the settlement requires a rifle.
highlights: Polar night from late October to mid-February, and midnight sun from April
The global seed vault, seen from outside only

cities.name: Røros
cities.why: A 17th-century copper-mining town of black timber houses, at -30°C for weeks at a stretch and listed by UNESCO for surviving intact.
highlights: Slaggveien: turf-roofed miners' cottages on slag heaps
The mine at Olavsgruva, 50 metres underground

cities.name: Trondheim
cities.why: A student city built around the northernmost medieval cathedral in the world, and the end of a thousand-year pilgrim path.
highlights: Nidaros Cathedral, the terminus of the St Olav Ways
The old wharves along the Nidelva, best from the Gamle Bybro

cities.name: Kraków
cities.why: The royal capital that survived the war, with Europe's largest medieval square and a Jewish quarter that is now a district again.
highlights: The Rynek and the hourly trumpet call that stops mid-note
Wawel castle and cathedral, where Polish kings are buried

cities.name: Zakopane & the Tatras
cities.why: A wooden mountain town under the only alpine range in Poland, with its own architectural style.
highlights: Morskie Oko, a lake under a wall of granite
The Zakopane style — timber villas designed as a national architecture

cities.name: Warsaw
cities.why: Eighty-five per cent destroyed in 1944 and rebuilt from Canaletto's paintings, with a Stalinist tower and glass towers around it.
highlights: POLIN, the museum of a thousand years of Polish Jews
The Warsaw Rising Museum, loud and unsparing

cities.name: Białowieża
cities.why: The last primeval lowland forest in Europe, with wild bison in it, on the Belarusian border.
highlights: The strict reserve, entered only with a licensed guide
European bison — some 600 of them, wild

cities.name: Gdańsk
cities.why: A Hanseatic port of narrow gabled houses, where the war began and Solidarity ended it.
highlights: Długi Targ and the crane on the waterfront
The European Solidarity Centre at the shipyard gate

cities.name: Évora
cities.why: A walled town with a Roman temple in the middle, a chapel of bones, and megaliths in the fields around it.
highlights: The Temple of Diana, standing since the 1st century
The Capela dos Ossos and its unambiguous doorway inscription

cities.name: Lagos & the Algarve
cities.why: Golden cliffs, sea caves and the harbour that launched the age of exploration — and, less proudly, Europe's first slave market.
highlights: Ponta da Piedade's arches and grottoes by kayak
The Rota Vicentina north into the wild west coast

cities.name: Lisbon
cities.why: A tiled, hilly, sea-facing capital rebuilt on a grid after the 1755 earthquake, with trams that still climb the old parts.
highlights: The Gulbenkian, one of the best private collections ever assembled, in a garden
Jerónimos monastery's Manueline cloister at Belém

cities.name: Sintra
cities.why: A microclimate of mist and forest on a ridge, with romantic palaces built into it by people with too much money.
highlights: Pena Palace, painted in colours that should not work
Quinta da Regaleira's initiation well, a spiral into the ground

cities.name: Pinhão & the Douro valley
cities.why: Terraced schist vineyards falling into a dammed river, worked by hand because machines cannot stand up on them.
highlights: The Douro railway along the water from Peso da Régua
Quintas that take guests and let you pick during harvest

cities.name: Porto
cities.why: Steep, granite and blue-tiled, with port lodges across the river and an ocean at the end of the tram line.
highlights: Livraria Lello, and the queue that proves it
Port lodges in Vila Nova de Gaia, tasted in order

cities.name: Bucharest
cities.why: Belle Époque boulevards, communist megastructures, and the second-largest administrative building on earth.
highlights: The Palace of the Parliament, which required demolishing a fifth of the old city
The Village Museum: 300 relocated buildings in a park

cities.name: Tulcea & the Danube Delta
cities.why: The gateway to 5,800 square kilometres of reed, channel and lake, with 300 bird species and villages reachable only by boat.
highlights: Pelican colonies, the largest outside Africa
Fishing villages with no road access at all

cities.name: Gura Humorului & the painted monasteries
cities.why: The base for a group of 15th- and 16th-century monasteries frescoed on the outside walls and still bright.
highlights: Voroneț's blue, a pigment nobody has fully reproduced
Sucevița's Ladder of Virtue, thirty rungs across a wall

cities.name: Săpânța & Maramureș
cities.why: Wooden churches with tall shingled spires, and a cemetery where every headstone is painted, rhymed and often rude.
highlights: The Merry Cemetery: 800 carved oak crosses with verses about the dead
Wooden churches on the UNESCO list, built without nails

cities.name: Brașov
cities.why: A Saxon town under a wooded mountain, with the largest gothic church between Vienna and Istanbul.
highlights: The Black Church, and its collection of Anatolian carpets
Tâmpa mountain, straight up behind the square

cities.name: Sighișoara
cities.why: A walled Saxon citadel still lived in, with a clock tower and a covered stairway to a hilltop school.
highlights: The clock tower's figures, turning since 1648
The covered stairway, 175 steps, built so children could get to school in snow

cities.name: Viscri
cities.why: A single-street Saxon village with a fortified church, horses on the road, and no through traffic.
highlights: The fortified church, whitewashed, on the UNESCO list
Hay meadows with some of the richest plant diversity in Europe

cities.name: City of San Marino
cities.why: A walled town at 750 metres with three towers along the crest and the Adriatic visible on a clear day.
highlights: The Passo delle Streghe, the path linking the first two towers along the cliff
Guaita, the oldest tower, from the 11th century

cities.name: Belgrade
cities.why: A fortress above the confluence of the Sava and the Danube, with floating clubs below it and brutalist New Belgrade opposite.
highlights: Kalemegdan fortress at sunset over the two rivers
Splavovi — river barges that are bars and clubs, all summer

cities.name: Novi Sad
cities.why: A Habsburg river city under the Petrovaradin fortress, with wine hills behind it.
highlights: Petrovaradin's fortress and its 16 km of underground galleries
Fruška Gora: sixteen monasteries in a wooded ridge

cities.name: Mokra Gora
cities.why: A mountain village on the Šargan Eight, a narrow-gauge line that climbs a figure of eight to gain height.
highlights: The Šargan Eight, 22 tunnels in 15 kilometres
Drvengrad, a wooden village built as a film set and kept

cities.name: Studenica
cities.why: A 12th-century monastery of white marble in a wooded valley, with frescoes from 1209 and monks still living there.
highlights: The Crucifixion fresco, a landmark of Byzantine painting
White marble churches inside a circular wall

cities.name: Bratislava
cities.why: A compact old town under a white castle, with a communist-era bridge and a UFO on top of it.
highlights: The castle and the view down the Danube into Austria
The blue church, Art Nouveau and genuinely blue

cities.name: Levoča & the Spiš
cities.why: A walled medieval town with the tallest wooden altar in the world, under the ruins of Spiš castle.
highlights: Master Pavol's altar, 18.6 metres of carved lime wood
Spiš castle, four hectares of ruin on a limestone hill

cities.name: Poprad & the High Tatras
cities.why: The gateway town to a 26-kilometre range that reaches 2,655 metres and behaves like the Alps.
highlights: Chata pri Zelenom plese and the hut network above the tree line
The electric railway from Poprad to Štrbské Pleso

cities.name: Bled
cities.why: An island church in a glacial lake under a cliff-top castle — the most photographed thing in the country and still lovely at 7 am.
highlights: Rowing to the island in a pletna, and ringing the wishing bell
The 6 km lakeside path, flat and swimmable at intervals

cities.name: Bovec & the Soča
cities.why: An alpine valley on an unreally turquoise river, and the front line of the Isonzo battles above it.
highlights: Rafting and kayaking on the Soča in early summer
The Walk of Peace: open-air museums along the 1915–17 front

cities.name: Ljubljana
cities.why: A capital of 300,000 with a car-free centre, a castle on the hill and Plečnik's architecture holding it together.
highlights: Plečnik's bridges, market colonnade and library — one architect's whole city
The riverside bars on summer evenings

cities.name: Piran
cities.why: A Venetian town on a spit, with a salt pan beside it worked the same way since the 14th century.
highlights: Tartini square, and the campanile modelled on San Marco
Sečovlje salt pans, harvested by hand

cities.name: Postojna & Škocjan
cities.why: Twenty-four kilometres of cave entered by underground train, and a canyon inside a mountain nearby.
highlights: The cave railway, running since 1872
Olms — blind cave salamanders that live a century

cities.name: Cádiz
cities.why: Possibly the oldest continuously inhabited city in western Europe, on a spit, surrounded by water on three sides.
highlights: La Caleta beach between two castles, in the middle of the old town
Carnival in February, which is the best in mainland Spain

cities.name: Córdoba
cities.why: The largest city in the world in the 10th century, with a mosque-cathedral of 856 columns at its centre.
highlights: The Mezquita, a cathedral inserted into a mosque and both left standing
Patio courtyards, opened to the public each May

cities.name: Granada
cities.why: The last Moorish city in Spain, under the Sierra Nevada, with the Alhambra above it.
highlights: The Alhambra's Nasrid palaces, booked months ahead and worth every minute
The Albaicín's white lanes and the view from San Nicolás at sunset

cities.name: Málaga
cities.why: A port that spent a decade turning itself into a museum city, with Picasso's birthplace and a Moorish fortress above.
highlights: The Picasso Museum, in the city he left at ten
The Alcazaba and Gibralfaro, walked up in half an hour

cities.name: Ronda
cities.why: A town split by a 120-metre gorge with an 18th-century bridge across it, in the middle of white-village country.
highlights: The Puente Nuevo, and the path down into the gorge below it
One of Spain's oldest bullrings, whether or not you approve

cities.name: Seville
cities.why: Orange trees, the world's largest gothic cathedral, and flamenco that belongs to specific families.
highlights: The Real Alcázar, still a working royal palace
The Giralda, a minaret with a cathedral built round it

cities.name: Albarracín
cities.why: A pink town wrapped in a river bend and a wall that climbs the ridge above it, in one of Europe's emptiest provinces.
highlights: The wall walk, up the hill and back down
Prehistoric rock shelters in the pine woods outside

cities.name: Torla & Ordesa
cities.why: A stone village at the mouth of a glacial canyon, under the third-highest peak in the Pyrenees.
highlights: Ordesa canyon and the Cola de Caballo, a full day on a good path
Monte Perdido, 3,355 metres, and the bearded vultures over it

cities.name: Zaragoza
cities.why: Roman, Moorish, Christian and industrial in the same city, with a basilica the size of a cathedral on the Ebro.
highlights: The Aljafería, an 11th-century Moorish palace, now the regional parliament
Basílica del Pilar's eleven domes on the river

cities.name: Ciutadella, Menorca
cities.why: Menorca's old capital: a sandstone harbour town on an island that is a UNESCO biosphere reserve and mostly farmland.
highlights: Camí de Cavalls: 185 km of bridle path round the whole coast
Talayotic stone monuments, on the UNESCO list since 2023

cities.name: Palma de Mallorca
cities.why: A cathedral with a Gaudí interior on the harbour, and the Tramuntana mountains behind it for the other three seasons.
highlights: La Seu, whose canopy Gaudí redesigned and whose chapel Barceló repainted in 2007
The Serra de Tramuntana, UNESCO-listed, and best from October to May

cities.name: Barcelona
cities.why: A Roman city inside a medieval city inside a 19th-century grid, with Gaudí's work scattered across all three.
highlights: The Sagrada Família's interior light, which is the actual point
The Eixample grid and its chamfered corners, a 19th-century plan that worked

cities.name: Girona & the Empordà
cities.why: A walled river city with the widest gothic nave in the world, forty minutes from Barcelona and a fraction of the crowd.
highlights: The Jewish quarter, one of Europe's best preserved
The city walls, walkable, with the Pyrenees on the horizon

cities.name: Tarragona
cities.why: The Roman capital of Hispania, with an amphitheatre on the beach and an aqueduct in the woods.
highlights: The amphitheatre, looking straight out to sea
Les Ferreres aqueduct, walkable along the top

cities.name: Valencia
cities.why: A river turned into a nine-kilometre park, a gothic silk exchange, and the actual home of paella.
highlights: Turia gardens: a flood-diverted riverbed, now the city's spine
La Lonja, a gothic trading hall with twisted stone columns

cities.name: Cáceres
cities.why: A walled old town of Moorish towers and conquistador palaces, with storks nesting on most of them.
highlights: A UNESCO old town with no modern buildings inside the walls at all
Storks on every tower from February

cities.name: Mérida
cities.why: The best Roman ruins in Spain, including a theatre that still stages classical drama every summer.
highlights: The theatre, from 15 BC, with a summer festival on its stage
A 792-metre Roman bridge, still walked across

cities.name: Bilbao
cities.why: A steel city that commissioned one building in 1997 and changed what cities thought was possible.
highlights: The Guggenheim, and the argument about whether one building can do that
Pintxos in the Casco Viejo, standing, one per bar

cities.name: Picos de Europa (Cangas de Onís)
cities.why: Limestone peaks twenty kilometres from the sea, with a cable car, gorges and blue cheese aged in caves.
highlights: The Cares gorge, twelve kilometres cut into a cliff
Cabrales cheese, matured in mountain caves

cities.name: Ribeira Sacra
cities.why: Vineyards on canyon walls above the Sil, worked from boats and by hand, with Romanesque monasteries in the woods.
highlights: Terraces at gradients that need a winch, above a 500-metre gorge
Mencía reds from vines nobody can mechanise

cities.name: San Sebastián
cities.why: A shell-shaped bay, a belle époque town, and more Michelin stars per head than anywhere on earth.
highlights: Pintxos bar to pintxos bar in the Parte Vieja, one dish each
La Concha beach and the walk round to Ondarreta

cities.name: Santiago de Compostela
cities.why: The end of the Camino: a granite city that rains constantly and fills each afternoon with people who have walked there.
highlights: The pilgrims' mass, and the botafumeiro when it swings
Arriving on foot into the Praza do Obradoiro

cities.name: Cuenca
cities.why: Houses hanging over a gorge on two sides, with an abstract art museum inside them.
highlights: The casas colgadas, cantilevered over a 100-metre drop
Spanish Abstract Art Museum, in the hanging houses themselves

cities.name: Madrid
cities.why: A high plateau capital with three of the world's great galleries in one kilometre and a nightlife that starts at midnight.
highlights: The Prado's Velázquez and Goya, and the Reina Sofía's Guernica
El Rastro flea market on Sunday morning

cities.name: Salamanca
cities.why: A university city since 1218, in sandstone that turns gold at sunset, with two cathedrals joined together.
highlights: The Plaza Mayor, the best in Spain and used as a living room
The frog carved on the university facade, which students must find

cities.name: Segovia
cities.why: A Roman aqueduct of 167 arches, built without mortar, running straight through the middle of a working town.
highlights: The aqueduct, 28 metres high, dry-stone, still standing after 2,000 years
The Alcázar on its rock, which Disney is said to have borrowed

cities.name: Toledo
cities.why: A city on a granite outcrop in a river loop, where Christian, Jewish and Muslim Spain were one place for centuries.
highlights: El Greco's Burial of the Count of Orgaz, in the church it was painted for
Synagogues built by Muslim craftsmen for Jewish congregations under Christian kings

cities.name: Malmö
cities.why: Post-industrial, young, and twenty minutes by train from Copenhagen across the bridge.
highlights: The Turning Torso and the Western Harbour rebuilt from shipyards
Falafel, which Malmö does better than anywhere north of Beirut

cities.name: Ystad
cities.why: Half-timbered market town on a long empty beach, with a Bronze Age stone ship on the cliff above.
highlights: Ales stenar: 59 boulders in the shape of a ship, on a headland
Three hundred half-timbered houses, still lived in

cities.name: Stockholm
cities.why: Water on every side, a preserved medieval core, and the best-funded museums in the Nordics.
highlights: The Vasa: a warship that sank in 1628, raised whole in 1961
Gamla Stan early, before the tour groups, or late

cities.name: Uppsala
cities.why: Sweden's oldest university, its largest cathedral, and the burial mounds of kings who predate both.
highlights: Gamla Uppsala's royal mounds, from the 6th century
The cathedral, the tallest in the Nordics

cities.name: Abisko
cities.why: A rain-shadowed valley with Sweden's clearest winter skies and the northern end of its greatest trail.
highlights: The Aurora Sky Station, reached by chairlift in the dark
Kungsleden: 440 km south to Hemavan, hut to hut

cities.name: Kiruna
cities.why: An iron-ore town so successful at mining that it is being physically moved, building by building, off the hole it dug.
highlights: The mine tour, 540 metres down
The wooden church, voted Sweden's finest building and relocated whole

cities.name: Bern
cities.why: The federal capital: six kilometres of arcades, a river you swim down, and Einstein's flat above a café.
highlights: Swimming the Aare with the current, as the city does all summer
The Zytglogge clock's mechanism, from 1530

cities.name: Lauterbrunnen
cities.why: A valley with vertical walls and seventy-two waterfalls, and car-free villages on the shelves above it.
highlights: Mürren and Gimmelwald, reachable only by cable car or on foot
Trümmelbach: ten glacier waterfalls inside the mountain

cities.name: St. Moritz & the Engadin
cities.why: A high valley of lakes at 1,800 metres, with sgraffito villages and 322 days of sun a year.
highlights: The Bernina Express over a UNESCO-listed railway to Italy
Segantini's paintings where he painted them

cities.name: Lugano
cities.why: Palm trees, a glacial lake and Italian spoken everywhere, twenty minutes from the Alps.
highlights: Monte Brè and Monte San Salvatore by funicular
The lakeside promenade and the ferries to Gandria

cities.name: Zermatt
cities.why: A car-free village under the most photographed mountain on earth, with skiing possible in July.
highlights: The Matterhorn from the Riffelsee at sunrise, reflected
Gornergrat railway to 3,089 metres

cities.name: Fethiye & the Lycian coast
cities.why: Rock-cut tombs in the cliffs above a harbour, and a 540-kilometre coastal path starting nearby.
highlights: The Lycian Way, hugging the coast for 540 km
Sunken ruins in the shallows off Kekova, seen from a boat

cities.name: Selçuk & Ephesus
cities.why: A market town beside one of the best-preserved classical cities in the Mediterranean.
highlights: Ephesus's library facade and marble street
The terrace houses, roofed and separately ticketed, with intact mosaics

cities.name: Göreme, Cappadocia
