cities.why: Soft volcanic rock eroded into cones and carved out for a thousand years into churches, houses and underground cities.
highlights: Rock-cut churches with Byzantine frescoes in the open-air museum
Derinkuyu, an underground city eighteen storeys deep

cities.name: Edirne
cities.why: The Ottoman capital before Istanbul, in the European corner, with Sinan's masterpiece mosque in it.
highlights: Selimiye Mosque, which its architect called his best work at 86
The oil wrestling championship each summer, running since 1362

cities.name: Istanbul
cities.why: Capital of two empires, on two continents, with a 1,500-year-old church-mosque at the centre of it.
highlights: Hagia Sophia, and the Basilica Cistern under the street outside
The Süleymaniye mosque, quieter and better proportioned than the Blue Mosque

cities.name: Canterbury
cities.why: The mother church of a global communion, in a walled town on the pilgrims' road from London.
highlights: The cathedral, and the spot where Becket was killed in 1170
The Pilgrims' Way, still walkable from Winchester or Southwark

cities.name: London
cities.why: A city of villages that grew together, with the free national collections of a former empire in the middle of it.
highlights: The British Museum, the National Gallery and the Tates — all free, all enormous
Borough Market, then the Thames path east past Shakespeare's Globe

cities.name: Belfast
cities.why: A Victorian industrial city working through its own recent past in public, with murals as the text.
highlights: The Titanic Quarter, on the slipway where she was built
Black cab tours of the peace walls, given by people who lived it

cities.name: The Causeway Coast (Bushmills)
cities.why: Forty thousand basalt columns, a rope bridge to a fishing rock, and cliffs the whole way along.
highlights: The Giant's Causeway, best at dawn or in rain
Carrick-a-Rede rope bridge, if heights are your thing

cities.name: Edinburgh
cities.why: A medieval spine running down from a castle on a plug of volcanic rock, with a Georgian grid alongside.
highlights: The Royal Mile at seven in the morning, before anyone else
Arthur's Seat, a full hill inside the city

cities.name: Islay
cities.why: A low green island of nine working distilleries, 3,000 people and 50,000 wintering geese.
highlights: Peated whisky at the distillery that made it, on the shore
Barnacle geese arriving from Greenland each October

cities.name: Isle of Skye (Portree)
cities.why: Black basalt ridges, sea cliffs and more visitors than the single-track roads were built for.
highlights: The Quiraing, a landslip you walk into
The Cuillin ridge, which is mountaineering rather than hiking

cities.name: Keswick & the Lakes
cities.why: A market town under Skiddaw on Derwentwater, at the centre of England's mountain country.
highlights: Catbells: a two-hour ridge with a view worth ten
Rowing on Derwentwater and the launch that circles it

cities.name: York
cities.why: Roman, Viking and medieval in the same square mile, inside walls you can walk around.
highlights: York Minster's medieval glass, the largest expanse in Britain
The Shambles, a 14th-century street of overhanging timber

cities.name: Cardiff
cities.why: A coal port turned capital, with a fantasy castle in the middle and a rugby stadium that empties into the streets.
highlights: Cardiff Castle's Victorian gothic interiors, wildly over the top
St Fagans: a free open-air museum of relocated Welsh buildings

cities.name: Eryri / Snowdonia (Betws-y-Coed)
cities.why: Slate, lakes and the highest mountains in England and Wales, in a national park with a Welsh-speaking heart.
highlights: Yr Wyddfa by the Watkin or Rhyd Ddu path rather than the crowded one
The slate landscape of Blaenau Ffestiniog, now UNESCO-listed

cities.name: Bath
cities.why: A Roman bathing complex under a Georgian city built in one honey-coloured stone.
highlights: The Roman Baths, still fed by the only hot spring in Britain
The Royal Crescent and the Circus, built as speculation and now the argument for it

cities.name: St Ives
cities.why: A Cornish fishing town whose light brought the modernists, and kept them.
highlights: Tate St Ives and the Barbara Hepworth garden, left as she had it
The coast path west to Zennor along granite cliffs

cities.name: Vatican City
cities.why: A state the size of a large park, holding Michelangelo's ceiling, his dome and his Pietà.
highlights: The Sistine Chapel, best at the first entry slot of the day
St Peter's dome, 551 steps, with the last stretch leaning inward
